s.d: to engage in continuous and repeated arguing
s.g: constant arguing; continuous arguing

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: the payment made to soldiers as ration money
s.g: pay; compensation

s.d: money which is needed for living expenses
s.g: money for support; money to live on
s.c: ὀψώνιον in ⟦2 Corinthians 11:8|2 Corinthians 11:8⟧ may be rendered as ‘money on which to live’ or ‘money for food and lodging.’

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ὀψώνιον<SDBG:ὀψώνιον:000000>}[a] ‘a soldier’s wages,’ {D:57.166}) the end result from some activity, viewed as something which one receives in return
s.g: wages; result

s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of a term meaning literally ‘to hunt,’ ‘to trap,’ not occurring in the NT) to acquire information about an error or fault, with the purpose of causing harm or trouble
s.g: to trap; to catch off guard; to catch in a mistake
s.c: In a number of languages it is possible to retain the figurative meaning of ‘trap’ or ‘catch,’ but in a number of instances other figures are used, for example, ‘to cause to trip,’ ‘to cause to fall,’ ‘to hear wrong words from his mouth,’ or ‘to use his words against him.’

s.d: a device used for trapping or snaring, principally birds
s.g: trap; snare
s.c: Since snares or traps for capturing birds are almost universal, there should be no difficulty involved in obtaining an appropriate term, though in the context of ⟦Luke 21:34|Luke 21:34⟧ the function of παγίς is figurative and clearly marked as a simile. It may be necessary in some instances to expand the simile somewhat as ‘as a snare is used to catch birds.’

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:παγίς<SDBG:παγίς:000000>}[a] ‘trap,’ {D:6.23}) that which brings or is a means of sudden danger
s.g: danger; trap
s.c: Though in ⟦1 Timothy 6:9|1 Timothy 6:9⟧ παγίδα and ἐπιθυμίας πολλάς are syntactically coordinate, the semantic relationship involves dependency, since the danger consists of the many foolish and harmful desires. One could translate, therefore, ‘the danger of many foolish and harmful desires’ or ‘the danger of being trapped by many foolish and harmful desires.’ In this way, something of the literal as well as the figurative meaning of παγίς may be retained.

s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:παγίς<SDBG:παγίς:000000>}[a] ‘trap’ {D:6.23}) an instrument or means for gaining control, implying an element of surprise
s.g: means of control; way of trapping
s.c: In a number of languages, it is possible to reflect something of the figurative meaning of παγίς by translating the term as a verb, for example, ‘may they be caught and trapped at their feasts’ or ‘may their feasts snare and trap them’ (see LN 6.23 and LN 6.24).

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: to suffer pain
s.g: pain; suffering; to suffer; to be in pain
s.c: In ⟦1 Peter 4:13|1 Peter 4:13⟧ the phrase τοῖς τοῦ Χριστοῦ παθήμασιν ‘in the sufferings of Christ’ may mean ‘the sufferings experienced at the time of the Messiah,’ that is to say, ‘the Messianic woes.’ See also LN 24.87.

s.d: to experience strong physical desires, particularly of a sexual nature
s.g: passion; lust; lustful desire; to have lust

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: pertaining to being subject to suffering
s.g: subject to suffering

s.d: to experience strong physical desires, particularly of a sexual nature
s.g: passion; lust; lustful desire; to have lust

s.d: a person who guides, directs, and shows concern for
s.g: guardian; leader; guide
s.c: It may be difficult to render appropriately ἐπίτροπος and παιδαγωγός with a combined meaning of guiding and caring for. It may, in fact, be necessary in some instances to use two verbal expressions, for example, ‘to guide and to help’ or ‘to help by leading’ or ‘to care for by leading.’|In classical times, a παιδαγωγός was a man, usually a slave, whose task it was to conduct a boy to and from school and to supervise and direct his general conduct. He was not a teacher.

s.d: (diminutive of {L:παῖς<SDBG:παῖς:000000>}[a] ‘child,’ {D:9.41}, but in the NT παιδάριον has seemingly lost at least most of this diminutive force, but may have retained some implications of affectionate concern or interest) a child, normally below the age of puberty
s.g: child
s.c: Note that παιδάριον in ⟦John 6:9|John 6:9⟧ denotes merely a child; it is the referential pronoun ὅς which indicates masculine gender, and therefore one may translate ‘boy.’|It is also possible that in this context the diminutive παιδάριον carries some connotation of endearment.

s.d: to provide instruction, with the intent of forming proper habits of behavior{N:001}
s.g: to teach; to instruct; to train; teaching; instruction

s.d: to train someone in accordance with proper rules of conduct and behavior
s.g: to discipline; to train; discipline; training

s.d: to punish for the purpose of improved behavior
s.g: to punish; punishment

s.d: (derivative of {L:παιδεύω<SDBG:παιδεύω:000000>}[a] ‘to train,’ {D:33.226}) one who provides instruction for the purpose of proper behavior
s.g: instructor; trainer; teacher

s.d: (derivative of {L:παιδεύω<SDBG:παιδεύω:000002>}[c] ‘to punish,’ {D:38.4}) a person who punishes for constructive purposes
s.g: punisher; one who punishes

s.d: to provide instruction, with the intent of forming proper habits of behavior{N:001}
s.g: to teach; to instruct; to train; teaching; instruction

s.d: to train someone in accordance with proper rules of conduct and behavior
s.g: to discipline; to train; discipline; training

s.d: to punish for the purpose of improved behavior
s.g: to punish; punishment

s.dp: Time › Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
s.d: the period from the time a person is a child until the time of the context{N:001}
s.g: since childhood
s.c: In παιδιόθεν, the stem παιδιο would suggest an age somewhat older than in the case of βρέφος ‘infancy’ (LN 67.152). παιδιόθεν, accordingly, would probably refer to a period of time which begins after a child has been weaned.

s.d: (diminutive of παῖς[a] ‘child,’ {D:9.41}, but in the NT παιδίον has seemingly lost at least most of this diminutive force, but may have retained some implications of affectionate concern or interest) a child, normally below the age of puberty
s.g: child

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: (diminutive of {L:παῖς<SDBG:παῖς:000001>}[b] ‘child,’ {D:10.36}, but with the loss of at least most of the diminutive meaning) one’s immediate offspring
s.g: child; offspring
s.c: One need not assume in ⟦Luke 11:7|Luke 11:7⟧ that the children were in the same bed with their father. One may render this passage simply as ‘I have gone to bed and so have my children’ or ‘I am already in bed and so are my children,’ but see LN 6.108.

s.dp: People › Persons For Whom There Is Affectionate Concern
s.d: (extension of meaning of {L:παιδίον<SDBG:παιδίον:000000>}[a] ‘child,’ {D:9.42}) a person of any age for whom there is a special relationship of endearment and association
s.g: my child; my dear friend; my dear man; my dear one; my dear lad
s.c: In a number of languages παιδία in ⟦John 21:5|John 21:5⟧ is better rendered as ‘my good friends’ or ‘my dear friends’ or ‘my dear comrades.’ In this context, not age, but the connotation of affection and endearment is in focus.

s.d: a female slave{N:001}
s.g: slave girl; slave woman

s.d: to engage in an activity for the sake of amusement and/or recreation
s.g: to play
s.c: The specific reference of παίζω in ⟦1 Corinthians 10:7|1 Corinthians 10:7⟧ is probably to dancing, but some scholars interpret παίζω in this context as a euphemism for sex.

s.d: a young person, normally below the age of puberty and without distinction as to sex
s.g: child
s.c: The term παῖς may occur with either masculine or feminine articles and corresponding adjectival attributes. These gender distinctions indicate whether the person referred to is male or female. With the masculine article or attributives one may translate παῖς as ‘boy,’ and similarly with female attributives one may translate παῖς as ‘girl.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: one’s immediate offspring, but without specific reference to sex or age
s.g: child; offspring
s.c: In languages in which there is no generic term for ‘child’ or ‘offspring,’ one may use ‘son’ or ‘daughter’ or ‘son and daughter,’ singular or plural, depending upon the context.

s.d: a slave, possibly serving as a personal servant and thus with the implication of kindly regard
s.g: slave

s.d: to strike or hit an object, one or more times
s.g: to hit; to strike; to beat

s.d: to sting (as of a scorpion)
s.g: to sting; to strike

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: pertaining to a point of time preceding another point of time, with an interval of considerable length{N:001}
s.g: long ago; of long ago
s.c: References to a point of time preceding another point of time may express a relationship to an event in the discourse or to the time of the discourse itself. In ⟦Hebrews 1:1|Hebrews 1:1⟧ πάλαι marks a point of time long before the actual writing of this Letter to the Hebrews. The same is true of ἔκπαλαι in ⟦2 Peter 3:5|2 Peter 3:5⟧. In some languages it is necessary to indicate clearly whether the interval is (1) between a prior time and the event mentioned in the discourse or (2) between a prior time and the discourse itself. For example, in ⟦Hebrews 1:1|Hebrews 1:1⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘long ago before now God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets’ or ‘long ago before now that I am writing …’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Unit of Time: During, In, While, Throughout
s.d: a considerable and continuous extent of time in the past
s.g: all this time; all that time

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time preceding another point of time and implying completion, but with a longer interval of time than in the case of {L:ἤδη<SDBG:ἤδη:000000>} ({D:67.20})
s.g: already; already for some time
s.c: The use of πάλαι in ⟦Mark 15:44|Mark 15:44⟧ would seem to suggest that Jesus‘ death had taken place considerably sooner than what Pilate had thought would happen. In trying to render the implication of πάλαι, it may be possible to translate ⟦Mark 15:44|Mark 15:44⟧ as ‘Pilate called the army officer and asked him if Jesus had indeed already died.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to having existed continuously for a relatively long time
s.g: old
s.c: παλαιός in a context involving wineskins focuses upon the use of such wineskins over a long period of time, and therefore it may be necessary in some languages to translate ‘used wineskins’ or ‘wineskins which have been used for a long time.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › New, Old [primarily non-temporal]
s.d: pertaining to that which is old, obsolete, and hence inferior
s.g: old

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: pertaining to a point of time preceding another point of time, with an interval of considerable length
s.g: long ago; of long ago
s.c: References to a point of time preceding another point of time may express a relationship to an event in the discourse or to the time of the discourse itself. In ⟦Hebrews 1:1|Hebrews 1:1⟧ πάλαι marks a point of time long before the actual writing of this Letter to the Hebrews. The same is true of ἔκπαλαι in ⟦2 Peter 3:5|2 Peter 3:5⟧. In some languages it is necessary to indicate clearly whether the interval is (1) between a prior time and the event mentioned in the discourse or (2) between a prior time and the discourse itself. For example, in ⟦Hebrews 1:1|Hebrews 1:1⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘long ago before now God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets’ or ‘long ago before now that I am writing …’|Though in some translations τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης is rendered as ‘the old covenant,’ it is important to distinguish in the meanings of ‘old’ between that which has lasted for a long time and that which comes from a period long ago. It is the latter meaning which is relevant in the context of ⟦2 Corinthians 3:14|2 Corinthians 3:14⟧.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: (an idiom, literally: old person, or: former person) the old or former pattern of behavior, in contrast with a new pattern of behavior which people should conform to
s.g: old self; old pattern of life
s.c: In a number of languages one can best render this expression in ⟦Ephesians 4:22|Ephesians 4:22⟧ as ‘don’t live the way you used to.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: the state of being old, with the implication of obsolescence
s.g: oldness; old; being obsolete
s.c: For a somewhat different interpretation of παλαιότης in ⟦Romans 7:6|Romans 7:6⟧, see LN 58.74.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › New, Old [primarily non-temporal]
s.d: the state of that which is old, obsolete, and hence inferior and unsatisfactory (in contrast with that which is either {L:καινός<SDBG:καινός:000001>}[b] or {L:νέος<SDBG:νέος:000001>}[b] ‘new,’ {D:58.71})
s.g: old; obsolete; old way

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to cause to become old and obsolete, and hence no longer valid
s.g: to make old; to make out of date

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to become old, with the implication of becoming obsolete and/or useless
s.g: to become old; to deteriorate
s.c: In some languages it may be useful to translate παλαιόομαι in ⟦Hebrews 1:11|Hebrews 1:11⟧ as ‘they will become old and worn out.’

s.d: to engage in intense struggle, involving physical or nonphysical force against strong opposition
s.g: to struggle; to fight
s.c: In a number of languages a marked distinction is made between physical fighting and nonphysical contending with someone. It is therefore often impossible to carry over any terminology involving war or physical struggling to contexts in which one is speaking of interpersonal hostility or contention.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: to experience a complete change in one’s way of life to what it should be, with the implication of return to a former state or relation
s.g: to be born again; to experience new birth; rebirth
s.c: The metaphor of ‘new birth’ is so important in the NT that it should be retained if at all possible. In some languages ‘new birth’ can be expressed as ‘to cause to be born all over again’ or ‘to have a new life as though one were born a second time.’ See also LN 13.55.

s.dp: Time › Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
s.d: an era involving the renewal of the world (with special reference to the time of the Messiah)
s.g: new age; Messianic age

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a subsequent point of time involving repetition
s.g: again

s.d: a marker of an additive relation involving repetition
s.g: and; also; again

s.d: a marker of contrast, with the implication of a sequence
s.g: on the other hand; but in turn; however

s.d: the totality of a relatively large group
s.g: all together

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a province in the southern part of Asia Minor
s.g: Pamphylia

s.d: a place for the lodging of travellers
s.g: inn

s.d: one who manages an inn as a place where people may obtain board and room at a price
s.g: innkeeper; manager of a hotel
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to describe the role of an inn or hotel as ‘a place where people could stay overnight and get something to eat’ or even ‘a place where people could pay in order to stay overnight and get something to eat.’

s.d: a gathering for a happy, joyous festivity
s.g: celebration; festivity; joyous festival
s.c: For the punctuation problem in translating the total context of ⟦Hebrews 12:22|Hebrews 12:22⟧, see commentaries.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Groups and Members of Groups of Persons Regarded as Related by Blood but without Special Reference to Successive Generations
s.d: consisting of all those who belong to the same family or household
s.g: together with an entire household

s.d: a complete set of instruments used in defensive or offensive warfare (usually, however, with emphasis upon defensive armament, including helmet, shield, breastplate)
s.g: weapons and armor
s.c: πανοπλία is also used figuratively in the NT as a reference to the virtues of Christian character used in the strife against evil: ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ θεοῦ πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι ὑμᾶς στῆναι πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου ‘put on all the armor that God gives you, so that you will stand up against the Devil’s evil tricks’ ⟦Ephesians 6:11|Ephesians 6:11⟧.|Since certain ancient types of armor are no longer used to any extent in fighting, it may be necessary to employ descriptive expressions in order to make clear the types of weapons and/or instruments which were involved. Offensive weapons are often spoken of as ‘tools with which one kills or harms an enemy,’ while defensive armor may be described as ‘what one wears to defend oneself when fighting.’ The complete sense of πανοπλία may then be described in some languages as ‘tools with which one fights against the enemy and what one uses to defend oneself’ or ‘… to protect oneself.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: trickery involving evil cunning
s.g: craftiness; treachery

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Licentiousness, Perversion
s.d: (literally: one who is ready to do anything) pertaining to being crafty and sly
s.g: scoundrel; crafty fellow

s.d: all possible positions
s.g: everywhere; anywhere; all over

s.d: all possible positions
s.g: everywhere; anywhere; all over

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: unlimited duration of time, with particular focus upon the future
s.g: always; forever; forever and ever; eternally
s.c: For another interpretation of εἰς τὸ παντελές in ⟦Hebrews 7:25|Hebrews 7:25⟧, see LN 78.47.

s.d: a degree of completeness, with the possible implication of purpose or result
s.g: completely; totally; entirely; wholly
s.c: It is also possible to understand the phrase εἰς τὸ παντελές as meaning ‘forever’ (see LN 67.95).|It is possible to translate this expression in ⟦Luke 13:11|Luke 13:11⟧ as ‘she could not straighten up at all.’ The difference of interpretation in ⟦Luke 13:11|Luke 13:11⟧ depends upon the scope of the phrase εἰς τὸ παντελές. If this phrase qualifies the negation, then the rendering is ‘she could not straighten up at all,’ but if the phrase εἰς τὸ παντελές qualifies just ἀνακύψαι, then the appropriate meaning would be ‘she could not straighten up completely.’

s.d: all possible positions
s.g: everywhere; anywhere; all over
s.c: The expression πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ in ⟦Acts 24:3|Acts 24:3⟧ is repetitive for the sake of emphasis. Some scholars, however, interpret πάντῃ in ⟦Acts 24:3|Acts 24:3⟧ as ‘at all times,’ in which case ⟦Acts 24:3|Acts 24:3⟧ would be a rare example of this meaning of πάντῃ in Greek.

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension From a Source
s.d: extension from a source, involving all possible points
s.g: from everywhere; from all directions

s.d: all possible positions
s.g: everywhere; anywhere; all over

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: a title for God, literally: all powerful
s.g: the Almighty; the One who has all power
s.c: In some languages the Almighty as a title for God may be expressed as ‘the one who controls everything’ or ‘the one who commands all things and all people.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: duration of time, with reference to a series of occasions
s.g: always; at all times; on every occasion

s.d: pertaining to being in every respect certain
s.g: certainly; really; doubtless; no doubt

s.d: a marker of strong emphasis, indicating complete validation of what is said
s.g: indeed; certainly; at all; at least; in any event

s.dp: Spacial Positions › At, Beside, Near, Far
s.d: a position near another location or object, usually with the implication of being alongside or close to
s.g: at; by; alongside; beside

s.dp: Spacial Positions › Among, Between, In, Inside
s.d: a position within an area determined by other objects and distributed among such objects{N:002}
s.g: among; with

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension From a Source
s.d: (with the genitive{N:003}) extension from a source which is actively involved in an activity or relation
s.g: from

s.dp: Case › Source of Event or Activity
s.d: (with the genitive) a marker of the agentive source of an activity, though often remote and indirect
s.g: from; by; of

s.dp: Case › Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
s.d: (with the genitive or dative) a marker of potential agent
s.g: by; for; with

s.d: (with the dative) marking a participant whose viewpoint is relevant to an event{N:004}
s.g: in the sight of; in the opinion of; in the judgment of

s.d: a marker of that which is contrary to what should be or to expectation
s.g: contrary to; opposed; not in accordance

s.d: a marker of contrast by means of an alternative
s.g: rather than; instead of
s.c: In a number of languages an alternative contrast must be expressed by a positive-negative sequence. For example, in ⟦Romans 1:25|Romans 1:25⟧ one may translate ‘they worship and serve what God has created; they do not worship and serve the Creator himself.’

s.d: a marker of association, with the implication of proximity to the so-called viewpoint character
s.g: with

s.d: a marker of cause or reason, with focus upon the source{N:005}
s.g: because of

s.dp: Degree › More Than, Less Than [Comparative Degree]
s.d: a degree which is beyond that of a compared scale of extent
s.g: more than; to a greater degree than; beyond

s.d: the state of being less than a given number or quantity
s.g: less; minus
s.c: In a number of languages it may seem strange as well as illogical to speak of ‘forty lashes minus one.’ Accordingly, one may translate ‘thirty-nine lashes’ in ⟦2 Corinthians 11:24|2 Corinthians 11:24⟧.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Groups and Members of Groups of Persons Regarded as Related by Blood but without Special Reference to Successive Generations
s.d: (an idiom, literally: those beside him) the associates of a person, including family, neighbors, and friends
s.g: his family
s.c: In some languages the idiom οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ is matched by other idiomatic expressions such as ‘those who share the same fire’ or ‘those who eat from the same pot.’

s.d: to act contrary to established custom or law, with the implication of intent
s.g: to disobey; to break the law; to transgress; disobedience; transgression
s.c: Languages differ appreciably in the way in which they speak of disobeying or transgressing a law. It is rarely possible to speak of ‘breaking a law,’ since nothing is actually done to the law in the process of transgression, but languages do employ such expressions as ‘to tramp on a law,’ ‘to ridicule a law,’ and ‘to laugh at a law.’ See also discussion at LN 36.29.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of παραβαίνω ‘to go aside,’ not occurring in the NT) to cease by removing oneself from some activity or position
s.g: to cease; to stop; to give up
s.c: In ⟦Acts 1:25|Acts 1:25⟧ διακονίας and ἀποστολῆς are the events to which παρέβη is related as aspect.

s.d: (a technical, nautical term) to sail up to or near
s.g: to approach; to arrive at; to sail to

s.d: to act contrary to established custom or law, with the implication of intent
s.g: to disobey; to break the law; to transgress; disobedience; transgression
s.c: Languages differ appreciably in the way in which they speak of disobeying or transgressing a law. It is rarely possible to speak of ‘breaking a law,’ since nothing is actually done to the law in the process of transgression, but languages do employ such expressions as ‘to tramp on a law,’ ‘to ridicule a law,’ and ‘to laugh at a law.’ See also discussion at LN 36.29.

s.d: (derivative of {L:παραβαίνω<SDBG:παραβαίνω:000000>}[a] ‘to disobey, to break the law,’ {D:36.28}) a person who customarily breaks or disobeys the law
s.g: transgressor
s.c: For terms involving ‘disobedience’ or ‘transgression,’ there are often a number of subtle distinctions reflecting several different types of contrasts. For example, there may be important distinctions between disobeying a person and disobeying a law or custom. A number of languages also make a clear distinction between intentional and unintentional disobedience or transgression. Another distinction may involve repeated activity or consistency of attitude, so that the choice of terms may specify whether a person has consistently disobeyed or has only disobeyed once or twice. A further distinction is sometimes made between disobedience of children or those who are mentally incapacitated and the disobedience of those who should know better. Accordingly, in the choice of terms for various passages of Scripture it is extremely important to note the distinctive features of meaning; otherwise, much of the emphasis upon disobedience and transgression as stated in the Scriptures may be seriously distorted.

s.d: to speak in such a way as to encourage a particular type of behavior or action
s.g: to urge

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Expose Oneself to Danger
s.d: to expose oneself willingly to a danger or risk
s.g: to risk; to risk one’s life
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘risking one’s life’ is ‘exposing oneself to death’ or ‘showing that one is willing to die’ or ‘walking into the danger of dying.’

s.d: a relatively short narrative with symbolic meaning
s.g: parable; figure; allegory; figure of speech
s.c: In almost all languages there is some way of speaking about parables or allegories. The equivalent in some languages may be ‘a likeness story’ or ‘a story that teaches’ or ‘a story that points the way’ or ‘words that have another meaning’ or ‘words that are saying something else important.’|Some scholars have insisted that in the NT παραβολή is used only in the sense of a story with one level of symbolic meaning, but in some contexts παραβολή is also used to identify allegories in which each element of the account has a symbolic significance. It is therefore extremely difficult to make a rigid distinction between parables and allegories.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Archetype, Corresponding Type [Antitype]
s.d: a model or example which anticipates or precedes a later realization
s.g: archetype; figure; foreshadow; symbol
s.c: In a number of languages it may be difficult to find a lexical item equivalent to ‘symbol,’ but one can often employ a relatively close paraphrase. For example, in referring to certain aspects of the tabernacle as being a παραβολή, one may render the first clause of ⟦Hebrews 9:9|Hebrews 9:9⟧ as ‘this says something to us about the present time.’ In other languages one may sometimes use a term which means ‘picture,’ for example, ‘this is a picture for the present time’ or ‘this contains some meaning for the present time.’

s.d: an idiom, literally: to place alongside a parable
s.g: to tell a parable; to utter a parable

s.d: pertaining to expressions which are not to be understood literally, but symbolically or figuratively
s.g: symbolically; allegorically; figuratively; so to speak
s.c: In a number of languages it may be more satisfactory to translate ἐν παραβολῇ and πνευματικῶς by a negative expression, for example, ‘not literally’ or ‘not really.’ The expression in ⟦Revelation 11:8|Revelation 11:8⟧ might be translated as ‘that city might be called Sodom, but it isn’t really Sodom.’

s.d: (derivative of {L:παραγγέλλω<SDBG:παραγγέλλω:000000>} ‘to order, to command,’ {D:33.327}) an announcement as to what must be done
s.g: order; instruction; command

s.d: to announce what must be done
s.g: to order; to command

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to come to be present at a particular place
s.g: to come; to arrive; to come to be present

s.d: to come to the assistance of someone
s.g: to come and help; to be present to help

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to come to be in a place
s.g: to come to be; to appear; to be in a place

s.d: to continue to move along
s.g: to move along; to go along

s.dp: Linear Movement › Pass, Cross Over, Go Through, Go Around
s.d: to move past a reference point{N:001}
s.g: to pass by; to go by

s.d: to go out of existence
s.g: to cease to exist; to pass away; to cease

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Shame, Disgrace, Humiliation
s.d: to cause someone to suffer public disgrace or shame
s.g: to disgrace in public; to put to shame
s.c: The expression ‘to disgrace in public’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘to cause everyone to think bad about’ or ‘to cause everyone to speak in whispers about.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Above the Earth
s.d: a dwelling place of the righteous dead in a state of blessedness (generally equated with {L:οὐρανός<SDBG:οὐρανός:000001>}[b] ‘heaven,’ {D:1.11})
s.g: paradise
s.c: In some languages ‘paradise’ has been translated by a borrowed term, but more often than not it is rendered by an expression which is roughly equivalent to ‘that wonderful place’ or even ‘that wonderful place in heaven.’|In ⟦Revelation 2:7|Revelation 2:7⟧ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τοῦ θεοῦ ‘in the paradise of God,’ the reference may reflect somewhat more closely the historical background of this term, which is derived from an Old Persian word meaning ‘enclosure,’ and thus was applied to a ‘garden’ or ‘park.’ For that reason, a number of commentators have believed that in ⟦Revelation 2:7|Revelation 2:7⟧, it is appropriate to translate ‘the garden of God,’ especially since in the context the reference is to the fruit of the tree of life.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to come to believe something to be true and to respond accordingly, with some emphasis upon the source
s.g: to accept; to receive; acceptance; reception

s.d: to accept the presence of a person with friendliness{N:001}
s.g: to welcome; to receive; to accept; to have as a guest

s.d: to hand over to or to convey something to someone, particularly a right or an authority
s.g: to give over; to hand over
s.c: In some languages, however, it is impossible to speak of ‘handing over authority.’ In some instances one may use a causative expression, for example, ‘to cause someone to have.’

s.d: to deliver a person into the control of someone else, involving either the handing over of a presumably guilty person for punishment by authorities or the handing over of an individual to an enemy who will presumably take undue advantage of the victim
s.g: to hand over; to turn over to; to betray
s.c: As is the case in English, a number of languages make a clear distinction between legitimate handing over of a presumably guilty person to a civil authority and the betrayal of a person in the in-group to someone in the out-group.

s.d: to pass on traditional instruction, often implying over a long period of time
s.g: to instruct; to teach

s.d: to grant someone the opportunity or occasion to do something
s.g: to grant; to allow

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to give into the hands) to hand someone over into the control of others
s.g: to deliver to the control of; to hand over to
s.c: In a context such as ⟦Matthew 26:45|Matthew 26:45⟧, παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας may be rendered as ‘will hand him over to be arrested’ or ‘will cause him to be taken into custody.’

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Expose Oneself to Danger
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to hand over life) to expose oneself willingly to a danger or risk
s.g: to risk; to risk one’s life
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘risking one’s life’ is ‘exposing oneself to death’ or ‘showing that one is willing to die’ or ‘walking into the danger of dying.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to give over the spirit) to die, with the possible implication of a willing or voluntary act
s.g: to die

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: pertaining to being difficult to be believed
s.g: difficult to believe; unusual; incredible
s.c: It would also be possible to translate εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον as ‘we have seen today things we can hardly believe’ or even ‘… things which people would scarcely believe.’ For another interpretation of παράδοξος in ⟦Luke 5:26|Luke 5:26⟧, see LN 58.56.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Unusual, Different From the Ordinary
s.d: pertaining to that which is unusual in the sense of contrary to expectations
s.g: unusual; remarkable
s.c: For another interpretation of παράδοξος in ⟦Luke 5:26|Luke 5:26⟧, see LN 31.44.

s.d: (derivative of {L:παραδίδωμι<SDBG:παραδίδωμι:000002>}[c] ‘to instruct,’ {D:33.237}) the content of traditional instruction
s.g: teaching; tradition

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Envy, Jealousy
s.d: to cause someone to feel strong jealousy or resentment against someone
s.g: to make jealous; to cause to be envious

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Bodies of Water
s.d: pertaining to being located beside the sea or along the shore
s.g: by the seaside; by the lake

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to fail to consider something sufficiently, and as a result, fail to respond appropriately
s.g: to overlook; to neglect; to disregard
s.c: It may be important to restructure this statement in ⟦Acts 6:1|Acts 6:1⟧ to read ‘because when help was being given out each day, their widows got nothing.’

s.dp: Help, Care For › Entrust To the Care Of
s.d: that which has been entrusted to the care of someone
s.g: what is entrusted; what is someone’s responsibility to care for

s.d: to indicate strongly to someone what he or she should plan to do
s.g: to advise strongly; to urge

s.d: to ask for with urgency, even to the point of demanding{N:001}
s.g: to ask for; to demand; to plead for

s.dp: Learn › Be Ready To Learn, Pay Attention
s.d: to not pay attention to
s.g: to refuse to pay attention to; to avoid; to pay no attention to

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: to refuse to accept one into a particular association
s.g: to refuse to accept; to reject
s.c: A strictly literal translation of παραιτέομαι in this context might be misunderstood, since it could suggest that younger widows were to be rejected from membership in the church. It may therefore be necessary to specify the particular relationships by translating ‘but do not accept younger widows in the list of those to receive support from the church.’

s.d: purposely to avoid association with someone{N:002}
s.g: to shun; to avoid; to keep away from; to have nothing to do with

s.d: to refuse to listen to and hence to disobey
s.g: to refuse to listen; to refuse to obey; disobedience
s.c: It would be a mistake to translate παρακούω, παρακοή, and παραιτέομαι as meaning nothing more than ‘not to listen to.’ The meaning is clearly ‘to refuse to listen to’ or ‘to refuse to pay attention to,’ and hence ‘to disobey.’ It may therefore be best in a number of instances to translate ‘to refuse to obey.’

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Sit
s.d: to sit down near or beside someone
s.g: to sit down by; to sit down near

s.d: to ask for something earnestly and with propriety
s.g: to ask for (earnestly); to request; to plead for; to appeal to; earnest request; appeal
s.c: It is also possible to interpret παρακαλέω in ⟦Acts 28:20|Acts 28:20⟧ as meaning ‘to call together’ (see LN 33.310).

s.d: to ask a person to accept offered hospitality{N:001}
s.g: to invite

s.d: to call to come to where the speaker is
s.g: to call together to
s.c: It is also possible to interpret παρακαλέω in ⟦Acts 28:20|Acts 28:20⟧ as meaning ‘to request’ (see LN 33.168).

s.d: to cause someone to be encouraged or consoled, either by verbal or non-verbal means{N:002}
s.g: to encourage; to console; encouragement

s.dp: Know › Not Able To Be Known, Secret
s.d: to cause something to be unknown or to be known only with great difficulty
s.g: to cause to not be known; to hide; to conceal; to make secret

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be present at a particular time and place{N:001}
s.g: to be present; to be here; to be there; to be at hand

s.d: to cause someone to be encouraged or consoled, either by verbal or non-verbal means{N:001}
s.g: to encourage; to console; encouragement

s.d: to ask for something earnestly and with propriety
s.g: to ask for (earnestly); to request; to plead for; to appeal to; earnest request; appeal

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for the Holy Spirit) one who helps, by consoling, encouraging, or mediating on behalf of
s.g: Helper; Encourager; Mediator
s.c: The principal difficulty encountered in rendering παράκλητος is the fact that this term covers potentially such a wide area of meaning. The traditional rendering of ‘Comforter’ is especially misleading because it suggests only one very limited aspect of what the Holy Spirit does. A term such as ‘Helper’ is highly generic and can be particularly useful in some languages. In certain instances, for example, the concept of ‘Helper’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘the one who mothers us’ or, as in one language in Central Africa, ‘the one who falls down beside us,’ that is to say, an individual who upon finding a person collapsed along the road, kneels down beside the victim, cares for his needs, and carries him to safety.|A rendering based upon the concept of legal advocate seems in most instances to be too restrictive. Furthermore, there may be quite unsatisfactory connotations associated with any word which suggests a lawyer, especially since in so many societies, a lawyer is thought of primarily as one who ‘bribes the judges’ or ‘can speak two truths’ or, as in one language, is ‘a professional liar.’ See also παράκλητος LN 35.16 and especially its footnote.

s.d: (derivative of παρακαλέω ‘to call upon to provide help,’ not occurring in this specific sense in the NT) one who may be called upon to provide help or assistance{N:001}
s.g: helper

s.d: to refuse to listen to and hence to disobey
s.g: to refuse to listen; to refuse to obey; disobedience
s.c: It would be a mistake to translate παρακούω, παρακοή, and παραιτέομαι as meaning nothing more than ‘not to listen to.’ The meaning is clearly ‘to refuse to listen to’ or ‘to refuse to pay attention to,’ and hence ‘to disobey.’ It may therefore be best in a number of instances to translate ‘to refuse to obey.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to conform in one’s behavior to a particular system of instruction or teaching
s.g: to follow; to be a follower of; to conform to

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of παρακολουθέω ‘to follow,’ not occurring in the NT) to make an extensive effort to learn the details and truth about something
s.g: to trace; to investigate carefully; to diligently check out

s.d: to happen in conjunction with some other happening
s.g: to happen along with; to happen at the same time; to accompany

s.d: to refuse to listen to and hence to disobey
s.g: to refuse to listen; to refuse to obey; disobedience
s.c: It would be a mistake to translate παρακούω, παρακοή, and παραιτέομαι as meaning nothing more than ‘not to listen to.’ The meaning is clearly ‘to refuse to listen to’ or ‘to refuse to pay attention to,’ and hence ‘to disobey.’ It may therefore be best in a number of instances to translate ‘to refuse to obey.’

s.d: to hear something without the speakers knowledge or intent
s.g: to overhear
s.c: Some scholars understand παρακούω in ⟦Mark 5:36|Mark 5:36⟧ as meaning ‘to ignore’ or ‘to overlook’ (see LN 30.37).

s.d: to not pay attention to something
s.g: to pay no attention; to ignore
s.c: Some scholars understand παρακούω in ⟦Mark 5:36|Mark 5:36⟧ as meaning ‘to overhear’ (see LN 24.66).

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Bend Over, Straighten Up
s.d: to bend over or stoop down, with the implication of looking into something{N:001}
s.g: to bend over; to stoop down

s.d: to look into something by stooping down{N:002}
s.g: to stoop and look into

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:παρακύπτω<SDBG:παρακύπτω:000001>}[b] ‘to stoop and look into,’ {D:24.13}) to make considerable effort in order to try to find out something
s.g: to try to learn; to desire to learn

s.d: to take or bring someone along with
s.g: to take along; to bring along

s.d: to take or lead off to oneself
s.g: to lead aside; to take aside

s.d: to acquire information from someone, implying the type of information passed on by tradition
s.g: to learn from someone; to learn about a tradition; to learn by tradition

s.d: to accept the presence of a person with friendliness{N:001}
s.g: to welcome; to receive; to accept; to have as a guest

s.g: to receive an appointment; to receive a task; to be assigned a ministry

s.d: to receive traditional instruction
s.g: to receive instruction from; to be taught by

s.d: (a technical, nautical term) to sail along beside some object
s.g: to sail along the coast; to sail along the shore

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Land in Contrast With the Sea
s.d: a territory bordering on the sea, in contrast with an inland area (compare {L:ἀνωτερικός<SDBG:ἀνωτερικός:000000>}, {D:1.65})
s.g: coastal region
s.c: Frequently παράλιος must be translated by a phrase, for example, ‘the land along the seaside’ or ‘the countries bordering on the sea.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: a change or variation in the nature or character of something
s.g: change

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mislead, Lead Astray, Deceive
s.d: to deceive by arguments or false reasons
s.g: to deceive

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: pertaining to being lame and/or paralyzed
s.g: lame; paralyzed
s.c: It is often best to speak of a paralytic as ‘one who cannot walk.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to suffer paralysis in one or more limbs, especially in the leg or foot
s.g: to be paralyzed; to be lame
s.c: In ⟦Hebrews 12:12|Hebrews 12:12⟧ παραλύομαι occurs in a highly figurative context: τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε ‘straighten up the paralyzed knees.’ It is often better in this context to speak of ‘strengthening the weak knees,’ but in any event, the reference to the physical situation of the individual is merely a way of speaking about a psychological state (see LN 25.152).

s.d: (an idiom, literally: straighten paralyzed knees) to gain encouragement by a strong resolve
s.g: to become encouraged; to encourage oneself by determination
s.c: See discussion at LN 23.170.

s.d: to stay in a place together with someone
s.g: to stay with; to remain with
s.c: In ⟦Philippians 1:25|Philippians 1:25⟧ παραμενῶ contrasts to some extent with μενῶ. The implication, in this particular context at least, is that the purpose of remaining is to serve the interests or needs of the believers in Philippi. It is also possible that some of this implication of serving may be found in ⟦1 Corinthians 16:6|1 Corinthians 16:6⟧.

s.d: to continue in an activity or state
s.g: to continue; to remain in; to keep on

s.d: to cause someone to become consoled
s.g: to console; to comfort; to encourage

s.d: (derivative of {L:παραμυθέομαι<SDBG:παραμυθέομαι:000000>} ‘to comfort,’ {D:25.153}) that which causes or constitutes the basis for consolation and encouragement
s.g: consolation; encouragement

s.d: (derivative of {L:παραμυθέομαι<SDBG:παραμυθέομαι:000000>} ‘to comfort,’ {D:25.153}) that which causes or constitutes the basis for consolation and encouragement
s.g: consolation; encouragement

s.d: to act contrary to established custom or law, with the implication of intent
s.g: to disobey; to break the law; to transgress; disobedience; transgression
s.c: Languages differ appreciably in the way in which they speak of disobeying or transgressing a law. It is rarely possible to speak of ‘breaking a law,’ since nothing is actually done to the law in the process of transgression, but languages do employ such expressions as ‘to tramp on a law,’ ‘to ridicule a law,’ and ‘to laugh at a law.’ See also discussion at LN 36.29.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Act Lawlessly

s.g: lawless act; evil doing

s.d: to rebel, with the implication of provoking to anger
s.g: to rebel; to rebel and provoke to anger

s.d: to rebel, with the implication of provoking to anger
s.g: to rebel; to rebel and provoke to anger

s.d: to abandon a former relationship or association, or to dissociate (a type of reversal of beginning to associate){N:001}
s.g: to fall away; to forsake; to turn away

s.d: to sail to and beyond a particular point
s.g: to sail past; to sail by

s.d: pertaining to being similar in the sense of almost equivalent to
s.g: very similar; closely resembling; almost the same as

s.d: pertaining to being similar in the sense of almost equivalent to
s.g: very similar; closely resembling; almost the same as
